experiment_data.hypothesis: Retry of binary_pairwise_001 (failed due to missing script on server). Dedicated binary RF for d3v4 and d4v5 pairwise AUC. Judgment: d3v4>0.75 + d4v5>0.75 → EDD≥5; d3v4>0.75 only → EDD=4.
experiment_data.notes: Binary pairwise RF (500 trees) on Pythia nucleus d0-d5 (30k samples, 5k/depth). Results: d1v2 AUC=0.9250 (vs 4-class 0.8607, +0.0643), d2v3 AUC=0.8225 (vs 4-class 0.8005, +0.0220), d3v4 AUC=0.7837 [0.7648,0.8024], d4v5 AUC=0.6832 [0.6611,0.7045]. Binary classifiers consistently outperform 4-class pipeline pairwise AUC (as expected, no decision boundary dilution). EDD=4: d3v4 above threshold (0.75) but d4v5 below. Feature extraction for d4/d5 done via Pythia-1.4B frozen model on LoRA-generated text. Top features shift from var_surprisal (d1v2) to p90_ppl/kurtosis (d3v4/d4v5), suggesting tail perplexity becomes the key discriminator at higher depths.
